_readme: Copy this file to ~/.agent/config.json and fill in your API keys.

providers._readme: api_format must be 'anthropic' or 'openai'. supports_vision controls whether image attachments are sent directly to the model. api_key can be a literal value or '$ENV_VAR' to read from environment. context_window controls the input context limit used by message compaction. Set higher for models with larger context windows. thinking.effort is optional and lives on the provider, not on the model, because the level is the provider's own word for it; see the deepseek block for what it accepts and what leaving it out does. stream_usage is optional too, and defaults to the opposite of thinking.effort: a streaming call asks the provider for its token report, because a stream that reports nothing cannot be measured or recorded; set it to false only for a gateway that rejects stream_options.

deepseek._thinking_readme: No 'thinking' key here on purpose, because leaving it out is the default: this provider is then asked exactly what it was asked before, and any thinking its models produce is still shown above the reply in an interactive turn (scheduled runs and sub-agents do not stream, so their thinking is recorded in history only). Add "thinking": {"effort": "low"} (or "medium"/"high") to ask its reasoning models for that much effort, or "off" to ask them not to think at all. A mixed group can set one model apart: "thinking": {"models": {"deepseek-reasoner": "high"}} overrides the provider's level for that model only, so the parameter reaches the model that understands it and not the one that would 400.

qwen._readme: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works — Qwen, Groq, Together, local vLLM, etc.

ollama._readme: Local Ollama — set api_key to any non-empty string (auth not required).

opencode-go._readme: Subscription gateways that want more than a URL and a key. headers is a name → value map sent on every request: a value of the exact form $NAME is read from the environment (same rule as api_key), and the token {session} is replaced per request with the id of the conversation asking -- one stable value per conversation, which is what x-opencode-session (and its like) means. Other placeholders are not substituted and are reported by config validation. User-Agent given here replaces the SDK's own.
opencode-go._max_tokens_readme: Placeholder: check this gateway's own docs for the model's output cap and context window before relying on them.

_max_tool_call_iterations_readme: Maximum model/tool exchange rounds in one turn before stopping as a possible loop. Values above the runtime cap are clamped; long workflows should make progress visible instead of raising this limit.
_output_reserve_readme: How much of the context window a request holds back for the answer, in tokens. This is NOT max_tokens: max_tokens is a ceiling on one response, while output_reserve is the room the conversation must leave free. Keeping them separate is what lets a provider be configured for long answers without shrinking its usable context -- deriving the input budget from max_tokens meant a 64000-token cap against a 128000 window left roughly 57k for the entire conversation. Set it per provider under providers.<name>.output_reserve, or here for all of them. The cap actually sent is derived per request as min(max_tokens, window - request - margin), so a request that nearly fills the window gets a smaller cap while a short one still gets the full max_tokens.

memory._readme: tidy_interval_seconds: how often (in seconds) the agent auto-reorganises memory. tidy_file_threshold: minimum number of new memory files before a tidy is triggered.

context._readme: Intelligent context manager. Split into 'storage' (what to keep) and 'consolidation' (when/how to compress).

_readme: max_categories: upper limit on dynamic LTM categories.
When exceeded, the agent merges two similar ones via LLM (default 15).
decay_factor: per-sleep importance multiplier (0.0–1.0, default 0.95).
Lower = faster forgetting. Entries below 0.05 are pruned automatically.
token_ratio: fraction of the provider's max_tokens at which a sleep cycle fires (default 0.70).
max_tokens itself is set in providers.<active_provider>.max_tokens — not here.
keep_last_messages: number of recent messages retained after sleep compression (default 6).
idle_seconds: seconds of inactivity before the background idle-consolidation task fires (default 300).
The idle task polls every 30 s and only triggers when the dirty flag is set (i.e. new messages exist).
min_messages: minimum messages in working memory before any consolidation is attempted (default 4).
model: model used for consolidation LLM calls (default: the active provider's model).
Set a cheaper/faster model here; consolidation runs in the background and never blocks a turn.
max_source_tokens: cap on how much staged text one consolidation run may read (default 8000).
max_chunks_per_run: staged chunks processed per run (default 2); higher drains backlog faster.
output_tokens: max tokens for one consolidation response (default 512).
staging_turn_threshold / staging_token_threshold: enqueue consolidation once the staging
buffer reaches this many turns (default 12) or estimated tokens (default 16000),
whichever comes first. Lower = memories persist sooner, more background LLM calls.
flush_on_session_end: on gateway shutdown, wait for pending consolidation to finish
instead of dropping it (default false). The trade-off: false keeps shutdown fast and
leaves staged turns to be consolidated on the next session use; true bounds shutdown
time by the slowest in-flight consolidation call.
token_estimation: ratios used to estimate token counts from character counts.
chars_per_token: non-CJK characters per token (Latin/ASCII, default 4).
cjk_chars_per_token: CJK characters per token (Hanzi/Kana/Hangul, default 1).
Increase chars_per_token for shorter English text or code-heavy sessions.
Increase cjk_chars_per_token if consolidation triggers too aggressively for Chinese/Japanese.
These are only the starting point: every provider response reports its exact input
token count, and the estimator calibrates itself against it during the session.
Calibration corrects an underestimate immediately (an underestimate means a call
hard-fails at the provider) and relaxes an overestimate slowly, so these ratios
rarely need hand-tuning. Images are priced at their provider cost, not base64 length.
Optional deterministic assistant identity bootstrap.
When set, these values are written into structured fact storage at startup so exact questions like 'what is your name' do not rely on free-form memory recall.

mcp_servers._readme: Remove this object and add real MCP server entries. Each entry needs name, command, and args.
mcp_servers.name: filesystem

evolution._readme: Self-improvement plugin. Set enabled=false to disable session scoring and behavioral rule learning entirely.

_readme: Persistent scheduled task service.
poll_seconds: how often the scheduler checks for due tasks.
lease_seconds: how long a claimed run is considered owned before stale-run recovery may requeue it.
Multi-agent orchestration bounds.
max_parallel_agents: how many sub-agents may run at the same time.
max_agents_per_turn: total sub-agents one turn may run, independent of concurrency; 0 derives it from max_parallel_agents (4x, minimum 8). A batch over the limit is rejected before any child starts.
sub_agent_timeout_seconds: total wall-clock budget for one sub-agent including all retry attempts.
sub_agent_retries: extra attempts for a transient failure, spent from the same budget. Read-only and research profiles only.
Optional speech-to-text command used by the built-in transcribe_audio tool.
Use {path} for the local audio file path and optional {language} for a language hint.
This is parsed as argv and shell operators such as ;, &&, |, and redirection are rejected.
Example: python /Users/you/bin/transcribe_audio.py {path}

plugins._readme: Per-plugin enable/disable. Use the plugin name as key. Set enabled=false to disable a plugin without removing it.

skills._readme: Per-skill enable/disable. Use the skill id as key (the directory name, e.g. 'skill-manager'). Set enabled=false to switch a skill off without deleting it; it then leaves the prompt's skill list, its slash command and activate_skill. Absent means enabled.

user_tools._readme: Disabled by default because ~/.agent/tools/*.py is trusted Python code executed in-process during startup. Set enabled=true only for tools you trust.

_system_prompt_file_readme: null = use the built-in prompt. Set to an absolute path to load a custom system prompt from a .md or .txt file, e.g. '/Users/you/.agent/my_prompt.md'.
_tavily_api_key_readme: Optional. Used by the built-in tavily_search tool. Can be a literal key or '$ENV_VAR'. Leave empty or null to disable Tavily-backed search.
_web_proxy_readme: Optional. Proxy for web_fetch, e.g. 'http://127.0.0.1:7897'. Needed on machines whose DNS answers with reserved addresses (Clash's 'enhanced-mode: fake-ip' does this): the direct path refuses those, so a proxy is the only way to fetch. null/absent = read the standard HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/ALL_PROXY environment variables (honouring no_proxy). 'none' (or 'off'/'direct') = always connect directly, ignoring the environment. Credentials are supported: 'http://user:pass@host:port'.
_output_dir_readme: null = use default ~/.agent/output. Set to an absolute path to override. Supports ~ and $ENV expansion. All tool/MCP/skill outputs (screenshots, exports, temp files) go here. Subdirectories are created on demand.
_shell_allowed_commands_readme: Persistent shell allowlist: entries that skip the confirmation prompt. A full command string (e.g. "ssh -o BatchMode=yes localhost whoami") matches that exact command; a bare command name (e.g. "osascript") allows every invocation of that command. High-risk commands (mkfs/dd/shutdown/… and shell control operators) require confirmation by default; adding them here lets them run without asking (the shell_blocked_commands blacklist still wins). Manage at runtime with /allow and /deny.

permissions._shell_level_readme: Default shell permission level for every session: ask = low/medium-risk run automatically, only high-risk (destructive commands/options, shell operators, pipe-to-shell patterns) asks for confirmation, and can run after approval (default); medium = high-risk commands/options/patterns also auto-allowed, operators still ask; high = everything auto-allowed (operators too) except shell_blocked_commands and structural guards; full = alias of high plus the only level that may combine with shell_sandbox=none. Change per session with /permissions <level>; persist the default with /permissions default <level>.
permissions._shell_sandbox_readme: OS sandbox for shell descendants: restricted = reads limited to system dirs + workspace/output; read_all (default) = reads open on the whole machine, writes still limited to output/workspace scope; none = no sandbox at all (danger-full-access, incl. GPU/Metal) and only valid together with shell_level=full. Change per session with /permissions sandbox <mode>; persist with /permissions default sandbox <mode>.
permissions._shell_secret_paths_readme: Extra home-relative paths the sandboxed shell may neither read nor write, on top of the built-in secret set (~/.aws, ~/.azure, ~/.gnupg, ~/.netrc, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.config/gh, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/Library/Keychains, and the agent's own home). Add ".ssh", ".docker" or ".kube" when this instance does not need git-over-ssh, docker or kubectl — they hold credentials but are excluded by default because denying them breaks those tools outright.
permissions._shell_devices_readme: Device/service access (Metal/IOKit/mach services) inside the sandbox. Open by default, matching the network posture, so local ML workloads (MLX/TTS/LLM) work without disabling the sandbox; set false for the strictest posture (reads/writes are still governed by shell_sandbox).

channels._readme: External channel configuration. Multiple channels may be active at once. If no channel is enabled the CLI is used by default.

_readme: Feishu/Lark bot via WebSocket long connection (no public IP required).
If running from the repo: uv sync --extra feishu && uv run simple gateway
If using a globally installed uv tool: uv tool install --reinstall --editable . --with lark-oapi
1. Create a Feishu app at https://open.feishu.cn/app
2. Enable 'Bot' capability and subscribe to 'im.message.receive_v1' event
3. Copy App ID and App Secret below
app_id / app_secret  : from Feishu Open Platform > Credentials & Basic Info
encrypt_key          : optional; set if 'Encrypt Key' is enabled in event subscription
verification_token   : optional; set if 'Verification Token' is enabled
allow_from           : list of open_ids allowed to use the bot; empty = allow all
react_emoji          : emoji reaction added when a message is received (THUMBSUP, OK, EYES, DONE …)
group_policy         : 'mention' = only respond when @mentioned; 'open' = respond to all group messages
Local HTTP/WebSocket API for the built-in React web UI and custom integrations.
Install: uv sync --extra web
Start:  uv run simple gateway, then open http://127.0.0.1:8787/.
Keep host=127.0.0.1 for local-only access. Set auth_token when exposing it
beyond localhost, and call /api/* with 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'.
cors_origins is only needed when a separate frontend dev server calls the API.
max_active_sessions: resident web sessions kept in memory (default 16). At capacity,
the least-recently-active idle session is evicted; its state is rebuilt from the
provider checkpoint on the next message, so eviction costs a replay, not the chat.
session_idle_ttl_seconds: idle sessions older than this are evicted eagerly (default 900).
A session mid-turn is never evicted, regardless of either limit.
